units.title: Actual fixed-spectrum precision reply conversion
units.reader_note: The two reply formulas are shown first; actual source matrices, domains, proof steps and exact Lean are folded below.
units.statement: For the same hidden rotation, either exact precision-matvec reply reconstructs its counterpart at the same query point.
assumptions: \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Both endpoints are included. Fix one arbitrary actual \(O\in O(d)\); both precision matrices use this same rotation, which remains the hidden input.

For source indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), define \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i(\eta)=(\eta+1)/2+(\eta-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and the actual matrices \(A_\eta=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1(\eta),\ldots,\lambda_d(\eta))O^\top\). Lean uses zero-based indices, so its angle is \((i.\mathrm{val}+\tfrac12)\pi/d\). The local formula is total in \(\eta\); the assertions use only source-valid \(\eta=\kappa\) and \(\eta=2\).
The actual reply is \(Q_\eta(x)=A_\eta x\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). The subscript 2 is the reference condition number, rather than a number of calls, a transpose query or a covariance inverse.

The scalar \(\kappa-1\) is at least one and hence nonzero; this is derived internally from the source parameter range. Orthogonality, the scalar/diagonal/matrix affine identities and both actual reply formulas are not additional premises.

The source experiment draws a Haar rotation independently of private randomness. The selected identity holds pointwise for every realization; this declaration does not assert a joint law, adaptive simulation, query cap, precision/cost comparison, Gaussian-target transport, or a separate formal spectral/positive-definite/normalizer theorem. The full fixed-spectrum lower bound retains its own fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\), sufficiently large \(d\), \(2\le\kappa\le d^{1-\delta}\) and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/10\) conditions.

notation.text: Actual precision reply at scalar parameter η; both κ and 2 use the same hidden rotation and deterministic angle grid.

steps.title: Align the actual cosine grid
steps.text: The zero-based coordinate i.val corresponds to source coordinate i.val+1. Derive positivity of d from the source dimension bound, then identify the two exact angle expressions. All matrices retain the same angle grid.
steps.lean: hdpos/hd0 derive a genuine nonzero denominator; hindex proves the exact source-index alignment.

steps.title: Lift the scalar affine identity to the diagonal
steps.text: Expand the literal eigenvalue formula at κ and at 2. The entrywise affine equality lifts to the diagonal matrix by comparing equal and distinct indices; no arbitrary scalar sequence or hypothesized matrix equality is introduced.
steps.lean: hscalar uses hindex and real polynomial arithmetic; hdiag proves the actual diagonal identity entrywise.

steps.title: Conjugate through the same hidden rotation
steps.text: Full orthogonal-group membership supplies OOᵀ=I. Distribute the actual matrix product and commute the known scalars through it. This yields the actual source precision identity with the same rotation on both sides.
steps.lean: hO applies the actual mem_orthogonalGroup_iff with explicit Fin d/real parameters. hmatrix consumes hdiag, matrix distribution, scalar multiplication and hO.

steps.title: Recover each actual reply
steps.text: Apply that matrix equality to the actual queried vector and transport its entries through the Euclidean representation. The forward formula gives a reply at κ from the reply at 2. Rearrange it and multiply by the genuinely nonzero inverse κ−1 for the reverse formula.
steps.lean: hforward uses WithLp.ofLp_injective, sub_mulVec/smul_mulVec/one_mulVec. hnz follows from hκ. The final inverse cancellation proves the reverse equality, with no totalized-zero shortcut.

steps.title: Compare two actual hidden inputs
steps.text: Instantiate the producer for O₁ and O₂ at the same x. Equal actual κ replies give equal actual reference-2 replies by the reverse maps; the forward maps give the converse. This is a genuine same-point observational consumer, separate from Gaussian target or algorithm-law transport.
steps.lean: Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumAffine calls the producer twice and applies congrArg to each known scalar/vector reply map.

units.lean_statement: Exactly the sealed source-domain, literal same-O cosine-grid, bidirectional actual precision-matvec reconstruction.
units.lean_proof: The exact complete production theorem is extracted adjacent to this formula proof. Every omitted standard bridge is internal; no abstract affine identity or reply-correctness premise is supplied.
units.boundary: Selected source S4.E11/Remark4.2 actual pointwise precision-matvec affine reconstruction in BOTH directions with the SAME hidden rotation, d>=2,kappa>=2, actual literal cosine-grid rotated matrices and actual Euclidean replies. A focused real consumer compares actual same-point replies for TWO actual hidden rotations. This does not establish Gaussian covariance/target-law/TV transports, operational adaptive/Borel transcript/seed/output simulation, deterministic/expected query or bit costs, finite-precision error adapters, the full fixed-spectrum spectral/PosDef/normalizer background, Krylov/moment estimates or either main lowerbound.
